lesson.grammar_point: wh- questions in the present simple and the past simple (what do you, what did you)

listenings.text: Hi, I'm Oliver, and I'm an HR director in London. I do about twenty job interviews every month, and I always ask the same three questions. First: what do you do in your current job? I want to hear the person describe a normal day. Second: tell me about a difficult moment at work. What happened, and what did you do? I ask this because I want to know how the person solves problems. And my last question is always: what questions do you have for me? A good candidate always has questions. When somebody says no questions, I am a little worried.

Hello, I'm Ingrid, and I'm from Gothenburg, in Sweden. Last year I had a job interview for a training manager position. The interviewer was very kind. She asked: what do you do in your current job? That was easy. Then she asked: why did you leave your last company? I was not ready for that question, and I talked for five minutes about my old boss. It was a mistake. The next day I sent an email to follow up and to thank her. I was on the shortlist, but I didn't get the job. Now I always prepare a short, positive answer for that question.
